proposals.before: Lu Fahe, minister of state, held Yingzhou and called in Qi. Tian was ordered west against him, but Fahe crossed north into Qi before he came up.
proposals.after: Lu Fahe, Minister over the Masses, held Yingzhou and called in Qi. Tian was ordered west against him, but Fahe crossed north into Qi before he came up.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is the Minister over the Masses (one of the Three Excellencies), not a generic minister of state.

proposals.before: When Wang Lin reached Dundu, Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were both lost in the river. Tian was made commander of the western campaign.
proposals.after: When Wang Lin reached Dunkou, Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu both fell into enemy hands. Tian was made commander of the western campaign.
proposals.reason: 並沒 here means both were captured (fell into the enemy's hands), not drowned; 沌口 is Dunkou.

proposals.before: When Wang Lin reached Dundu, Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were both drowned; Tian was then made Commander-in-Chief of the Western Campaign.
proposals.after: When Wang Lin reached Dunkou, Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu were both captured; Tian was then made Commander-in-Chief of the Western Campaign.
proposals.reason: 並沒 means captured/fell into enemy hands, not drowned; 沌口 is Dunkou.

proposals.before: In the first year of Tiancheng, second month, spring flood at Dong Pass let ships through. Lin brought Chaohu troops from Hefei downstream in a long line of war craft—the weight of it was immense.
proposals.after: In the first year of Tianjia, second month, spring flood at Dong Pass let ships through. Lin brought Chaohu troops from Hefei downstream in a long line of war craft—the weight of it was immense.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: That year he was ordered commander of Xiang, Ba, Ying, Jiang, Wu, and four other provinces, garrisoning Pencheng.
proposals.after: That year he was ordered commander of the five provinces of Xiang, Ba, Ying, Jiang, and Wu, garrisoning Pencheng.
proposals.reason: 五州 lists exactly five provinces; 'and four other provinces' is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: In youth he was close to Liang's left-rapid general Lan Qin and often campaigned with him.
proposals.after: In youth he was close to Liang's General of the Left Guard Lan Qin and often campaigned with him.
proposals.reason: 左衛將軍 is General of the Left Guard; 'left-rapid' misreads the garbled 衛.

proposals.before: Wei died in Tiancheng year 4, aged sixty-six.
proposals.after: Wei died in Tianjia year 4, aged sixty-six.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: In the Tiancheng era he was yellow-gate gentleman and extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant.
proposals.after: In the Tianjia era he was yellow-gate gentleman and extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: In Tiancheng year 3 he was made pacifier-of-the-west general.
proposals.after: In Tianjia year 3 he was made pacifier-of-the-west general.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: In the first year of Taijian an edict recalled him as left-rapid general.
proposals.after: In the first year of Taijian an edict recalled him as General of the Left Guard.
proposals.reason: 左衛將軍 is General of the Left Guard; 'left-rapid' misreads the garbled 衛.

proposals.before: Attendant-in-ordinary, bearer of the staff, director-general over punitive military affairs, campaign-north grand general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Duke of Nanping Commandery state Gong Mingche—heroic design achieved, grand strategy covering the age.
proposals.after: Attendant-in-ordinary, bearer of the staff, director-general over punitive military affairs, campaign-north grand general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Duke of Nanping Commandery-state, Mingche—heroic design achieved, grand strategy covering the age.
proposals.reason: 公 here is the ducal title (開國公), not a surname Gong; the person is 明徹 (Wu Mingche).

proposals.before: When Zhou extinguished Qi, Emperor Gaozong intended operations in Xu and Yan; in the ninth year an edict ordered Mingche to advance north on campaign, his heir Huizi, General of Martial Prestige in the Army and extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant, to hold provincial affairs.
proposals.after: When Zhou extinguished Qi, Emperor Gaozong intended operations in Xu and Yan; in the ninth year an edict ordered Mingche to advance north on campaign, his heir Huijue, General of Martial Prestige in the Army and extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant, to hold provincial affairs.
proposals.reason: 惠覺 is Huijue, as in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: Mingche's army reached Lüliang; Zhou Xuzhou overseer Liang Shiyan led Chen troops to resist; Mingche repeatedly defeated him; Shiyan withdrew to hold the city and dared not emerge.
proposals.after: Mingche's army reached Lüliang; Zhou Xuzhou overseer Liang Shiyan led troops to resist; Mingche repeatedly defeated him; Shiyan withdrew to hold the city and dared not emerge.
proposals.reason: Liang Shiyan was a Zhou commander; 率红 (for 率眾) means led his troops, not Chen troops.

proposals.before: He then donned armor himself, stormed the city on four sides, and took it at the first drum-roll; Wang Lin, Wang Guixian, Prince Fufeng Kezhuoluo Xiaoyu, Minister Lu Qian, and Left Director Li Taotu were captured alive and sent to the capital.
proposals.after: He then donned armor himself, stormed the city on four sides, and took it at the first drum-roll; Wang Lin, Wang Guixian, Prince Fufeng Kezhuhun Xiaoyu, Minister Lu Qian, and Left Director Li Taotu were captured alive and sent to the capital.
proposals.reason: 可朱渾 is romanized Kezhuhun.

proposals.before: Thereupon he personally donned armor, attacked fiercely on four sides; the city shook with terror; at one drum-stroke it fell; Wang Lin, Wang Guixian, Prince Fufeng Kezhuoluo Xiaoyu, Minister Lu Qian, and Left Director Li Taotu were captured alive and sent to the capital.
proposals.after: Thereupon he personally donned armor, attacked fiercely on four sides; the city shook with terror; at one drum-stroke it fell; Wang Lin, Wang Guixian, Prince Fufeng Kezhuhun Xiaoyu, Minister Lu Qian, and Left Director Li Taotu were captured alive and sent to the capital.

proposals.before: Merit and ability alone fit the supreme command; lofty banners and broad rewards are the constant rite—he is appointed director-general over Yu, He, Jian, Guang, Shuo, and North Xu, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and inspector of Yu Province, with three thousand five hundred households added to his pre-enfeoffment fief; the rest unchanged."
proposals.after: Merit and ability alone fit the supreme command; lofty banners and broad rewards are the constant rite—he is appointed director-general over Yu, He, Jian, Guang, Shuo, and North Xu, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and inspector of Yu Province, with his fief increased, together with the previous, to three thousand five hundred households; the rest unchanged."
proposals.reason: 增封并前三千五百戶 (赠前 is a garble of 并前) gives a combined total, not an addition before enfeoffment.

proposals.reason: 增封并前三千五百戶 (赠前 is a garble of 并前) gives a combined total.

proposals.after: Former attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works, Duke of Nanping Commandery, Mingche, from first treading on foot,

proposals.after: His courage was not Han Xin's or Bai Qi's, his wisdom not that of Sun Wu or Wu Qi—borders shrank, armies were lost, Jinling grew weak, and Zhenming fell, largely from this beginning.
